Bullies in Blue 2

By: Kate Barry | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A follow-up on the expose of rogue cops at Edenvale police station

Summary:
In July we exposed the various assaults on 3 different motorists at the hands of Constable Mapatlare of Edenvale SAPS. We follow up on what has happened to Goldtooth, the Station Commander as well as the national outcry to the story.

Further information:
We also bring new cases from Edenvale and other areas to show that this problem is widespread and is largely under reported. Motorists seem to be living in fear of the police and if they film their unlawful actions are subject to detention.
We also give viewers tips on what can be done when faced with a similar situation.

Press Release:


Bullies in Blue II
Several accounts relating to widespread police brutality came to the fore in the wake of Carte Blanche’s explosive investigation into alleged brutal assaults at the hands of Edenvale police officer Constable Derick Mapatlare – A.K.A ‘Goldtooth’. What has subsequently happened to the Constable and the Edenvale Police’s Station Commander? What can ordinary people do when threatened with assault or unjust arrest? Carte Blanche follows up on a story that’s caused a national outcry for action against rogue officers.


Script:


BULLIES IN BLUE 2

V/O: In July we brought you the story of rogue cops in Edenvale. Three complainants came forward with tales of abuse at the hands of the policeman with the gold tooth.

Gareth: When he hit me in the ribs, I automatically popped up again, and he hit me in the face. I can’t even tell you how many times he punched me in the arms.

V/O: Carte Blanche identified the gold-toothed bully as Constable Derick Mapatlare, but not even the Station Commander could identify his partner in the video.

Bongani: Do you recognize the other officer, the shorter one?

Eddie: I cannot see the face properly.

Link: Since our expose 2 weeks ago there’s been a massive response – especially on social media. We’ve been inundated with more submissions alleging further abuse. It would seem our story struck a nerve.

V/O: Thousands of people voiced their outrage and the issue became a topic of national discussion.

Yusuf: We need stern action; we need decisive action. When a policeman is implicated the first thing we would like to see is that cop needs to be arrested and charged.

V/O: Yusuf Abramjee is the Head of Crime Line, a national anti-crime initiative.

Yusuf: The quicker these rogue cops get arrested, the quicker we can set an example to the other policemen and women out there who are trying to abuse their powers.

Link: Within hours of our broadcast the Provincial Commissioner of Police vowed to take action against the officers concerned. Well it’s been 2 weeks – let’s see what’s happened.

Lesetja: We were met by the top brass of Gauteng – General Lesetja Mothiba - flanked by his Deputy Commissioners.

Bongani: Is Constable Mapatlare suspended?

Lesetja: He’s not yet suspended, we have served him with a notice in terms of our disciplinary regulations.

Bongani: What does that mean?

Lesetja: It means that we must give him the opportunity to respond to that. We gave him until last week Thursday.

Bongani: And now?

Lesetja: Now he has made representations, which means that any time from now a decision will be made. We also have served notice to the management of the Station to say “where were you when all these things were happening?” Because there is a Station Commander there, there are senior managers there.

V/O: Colonel Eddie Trollip, as well as Colonel Robbie Roberts were both served with suspension notices. But what about the criminal charges against Goldtooth?

Lesetja: The station did not do its work. That is why we have served the management with notice of suspension. They were supposed to have arrested to him. This case was supposed to be running in court.

Bongani: Have you identified the other officer in the footage from the hospital?

General: That is part of the investigation.

V/O: But it seems there are more rogue cops in Edenvale. In April this year Dylan Smith and his friends were pulled over near the N3. Dylan was in the passenger seat and started filming.

Benjamin: Are your windows locked?

Dylan: Mm…mm.

Dylan: We asked them for their names, any identity. They refused to give it to us. They said it’s none of our business.

V/O: When the cops realized Dylan was filming things got of out of hand.

Sfx: Eita, hey I don’t like what you are doing.

Dylan: He grabbed at both, at my arms and tried to drag me out of the car, he grabbed me around the neck and started pulling me out of the vehicle and eventually pulled the phone off of me.

V/O: Dylan and the driver were arrested and taken to Edenvale Police Station.

Dylan: There was a woman behind the counter who was shouting at me, saying I wasn’t allowed to record police officers, that is illegal, that I shouldn’t have been doing this.

General: I’m very much clear. If the filming is not interfering with a member of the SAPS in the execution of his or her work, then there should not be a problem with the filming.

V/O: But Dylan was charged with interference and locked up in the cells for the night. He managed to identify the arresting officers as Constables Rasekgoka and Khumalo. We showed this video to the Commissioner.

General: We will have to get the docket and see exactly what are the members are saying there. But of particular importance is that as the SAPS we are not having any policy to say we allow filming, we don’t allow it.

V/O: But when the Prosecutor saw the video evidence, he withdrew the case against Dylan.

V/O: Three weeks ago Renzo Bagattin was standing on the balcony of Cheerleaders sports bar in Edenvale, when he saw a policewoman allegedly assaulting a man in the parking lot.

Renzo: And I just saw her grab the guy by the back of his shirt like this, and swing him and smash him onto the bricks on the floor.

V/O: But when she and her partner saw him filming on his cellphone they rushed upstairs to confront him.

Renzo: I panicked, I tried to send the video and before I could the police officers were right next to me and snatched the phone out of my hand.

Bongani: What did they say to you?

Renzo: They said to me I’m not allowed to film police and they said they have to delete the footage.

V/O: When Renzo refused to give them his password he too was locked up at Edenvale Police Station.

Renzo: They said in a SA police station I have no rights and they will keep me there until Monday if I don’t give them the password to my phone.

V/O: After two hours Renzo surrendered the password. They deleted the video, and then gave him a lift home.

Renzo: The officer that arrested me, I saw on his badge was Marcus.

General: Bongani I think what we will have to do is call upon that particular member of the public to come forward, to lay an official complaint so that we can investigate.

Link: From the reports we’re getting from our viewers, it would seem the problem of police behaving badly isn’t just limited to Edenvale.

V/O: In June this year George and Stacey were returning from a dinner when they were stopped by the Soweto Flying Squad on the highway. Constable Wiseman Khumane insisted George was driving under the influence.

Owen: If I’m a police officer you must know boetie, I am the Boss of this road.

George: I think what really annoyed him is he saw that Stacey was filming the whole ordeal, recording it, and he said to me oh I see your wife is very clever. She thinks she’s very clever. We’ll show her how clever she is.

Owen: I’m a real police officer big man, you understand?

George: But are you annoyed because my wife…?

Owen: I’m not annoyed. I’m not annoyed. We must not speak together because I never asked her opinion. I’m speaking with the driver’s opinion. Do you understand me driver?

George: He said we should follow him to Baragwanath Hospital so we could go and have…they could take blood.

Stacey: We decided that we are going to rather go to the police station instead of following these guys. We will rather go to the police station because there I’m sure we will be safe.

V/O: They drove to Booysens Police Station, but when the Boss of the Road caught up with them, he arrested George.

Sfx: What is the charge……knock her over.

General: What this wife is doing is a clear case of interference. This is clear. When you film you don’t talk. If for example someone is being arrested you film, there’s nothing wrong with that provided you’re not going to say anything or take any action that will distract the members from that person.

V/O: But when Cathy and her friends were stopped at a JMPD roadblock on Witkoppen Road in May, she also got into trouble for filming.

Cathy: They’d come in in the window it was almost like they were trying to threaten him, but then they actually started tasering him.

V/O: This surprised Chief Superintendent Wayne Minnaar.

Wayne: The JMPD definitely is not using taser, and the officers are not issued with tasers, so this incident will definitely have to be investigated further.

Cathy: When they pulled him out of the car and I started recording them, that’s when they pushed him down on the ground and they carried on tasering him, kicking him and tasering him.

Sfx:

Cathy: She came and started hitting me, and hit the phone out of my hand and she was stomping and stomping on the phone.

V/O; Cathy was arrested by Officer Lerato Moanakoena. At Douglasdale Police Station she was charged with interference, and locked up.

Cathy: She was saying to me that I wouldn’t see my little one again, I must learn a lesson and us Whities must pay, and I said to her listen I have this on camera.

Wayne: We need to get both sides of the story. We’ll definitely need to investigate this incident further.

V/O: But as soon as the Randburg Prosecutor saw Cathy’s video, he withdrew the charges.

Link: It’s one thing to report police misconduct after the fact, but what do you do in the moment? What do you do when police pull you over in the middle of the night?

Lobo: Get onto the phone and give somebody your location so that somebody can come out and assist you. Keep your window as far closed as possible to still have communication with the policeman.

V/O: Lobo das Neves is a policing expert who recommends recording the interaction.

Lobo: There’s something that’s called What’s App. Do a recording and send it away immediately where it can be duplicated afterwards.

V/O: But most importantly the Provincial Commissioner is urging the public to come forward and report rogue cops.

General: Citizens of this country must make sure that even when someone is being violated that must be reported. It must be brought to our attention so that we can act on it.








BULLIES IN BLUE 2 PROMOS

Promo 1: 15”

Bongani: Sometimes the thin blue line the police represent the last barrier between order and anarchy, but from the reports we’re getting from our viewers it would seem the problem of police behaving badly isn’t just limited to Edenvale.

Promo 2: 15”

George: No let him do it, and my feet. You got another pair for my feet?

V/O: Tonight an update on the Edenvale cops, and more bullies in blue.



Promo 3: 10”

Cop: Eita, hey I don’t like what you’re doing.

Benjamin: But sir we have to do it. Watch the other side! Watch the other side!

V/O: Explosive new footage of bullies in blue.

Dylan: Don’t touch me! Don’t touch me!
